title_protection.quote: Using the designation Doctor, Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Osteopathy, physician, surgeon, physician and surgeon, Dr., M.D., or D.O., or a similar designation, or any combination thereof, in the conduct of an occupation or profession pertaining to the prevention, diagnosis, or treatment of human disease or condition

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of false, fraudulent, or forged statements or documents, or fraudulent/deceitful/dishonest/unethical practice in connection with certification or practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The use of any false, fraudulent, or forged statement or document or the use of any fraudulent, deceitful, dishonest, or unethical practice in connection with a certification, registration, or licensing requirement of this chapter

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conduct constituting a crime substantially related to the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conduct that would constitute a crime substantially related to the practice of medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Dishonorable, unethical, or other conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any dishonorable, unethical, or other conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing medicine under a false or assumed name.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter under a false or assumed name

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing medicine without a valid certificate or other authorizing document.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter without a certificate or other authorizing document or renewal of such document, unless otherwise authorized by this chapter

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use, distribution, or issuance of a prescription for a dangerous or narcotic drug other than for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The use, distribution, or issuance of a prescription for a dangerous or narcotic drug, other than for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertising the practice of medicine in an unethical or unprofessional manner.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Advertising of the practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter in an unethical or unprofessional manner

disciplinary_grounds.description: Soliciting or accepting a fee by fraudulent representation that a manifestly incurable condition can be permanently cured.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Solicitation or acceptance of a fee from a patient or other person by fraudulent representation that a manifestly incurable condition, as determined with reasonable medical certainty, can be permanently cured

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly assisting an unauthorized person to practice medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowing or intentional performance of an act which, unless authorized by this chapter, assists an unauthorized person to practice medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to provide adequate supervision to an individual working under the physician's supervision.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The failure to provide adequate supervision to an individual working under the supervision of a person who is certified and registered to practice medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Misconduct including sexual misconduct, incompetence, gross negligence, or pattern of negligence in the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Misconduct, including but not limited to sexual misconduct, incompetence, or gross negligence or pattern of negligence in the practice of medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful violation of the confidential relationship with or confidential communications of a patient.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Wilful violation of the confidential relationship with or confidential communications of a patient

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful failure to report malpractice information to the Board as required.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Wilful failure to report to the Board as required by § 1730(c) of this title

disciplinary_grounds.description: Unjustified failure to divulge information relevant to authorization or competence to practice medicine to the Board.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Unjustified failure upon request to divulge information relevant to the authorization or competence of a person to practice medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter to the Board

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of a provision of the chapter or a Board order or regulation related to medical procedures that will harm the public or an individual.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The violation of a provision of this chapter or the violation of an order or regulation of the Board related to medical procedures or to the procedures of other professions or occupations regulated under this chapter, the violation of which more probably than not will harm or injure the public or an individual

disciplinary_grounds.description: Charging a grossly exorbitant fee for professional services rendered.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Charging a grossly exorbitant fee for professional or occupational services rendered

disciplinary_grounds.description: Suspension, revocation, or other disciplinary action taken by a regulatory authority in another state or territory.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Suspension or revocation of a certificate to practice medicine or of the authorizing document to practice another profession or occupation regulated under this chapter, or other disciplinary action taken by the regulatory authority in another state or territory

disciplinary_grounds.description: Signing the death certificate of a person prior to the actual time of death.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Signing the death certificate of a person prior to the actual time of death of the person

establishment_regulation_required.quote: No person licensed under this chapter shall perform any office-based surgery, as defined in § 122(3)y. of Title 16, in a facility unless such facility is accredited or licensed in accordance with § 122(3)z. of Title 16.

definition_quote.value: "Practice of medicine" or "practice medicine" includes: (a) Advertising, holding out to the public, or representing in any manner that one is authorized to practice medicine in this State; (b) Offering or undertaking to prescribe, order, give, or administer any drug or medicine for the use of another person; (c) Offering or undertaking to prevent or to diagnose, correct, and/or treat in any manner or by any means, methods, or devices a disease, illness, pain, wound, fracture, infirmity, defect, or abnormal physical or mental condition of another person, including the management of pregnancy and parturition; (d) Offering or undertaking to perform a surgical operation upon another person; ...

drug_authority.value: Physicians may prescribe, order, give, or administer drugs or medicine; all prescriptions must be electronic except in specified exceptions; prescriptions for dangerous or narcotic drugs must be for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes only.
drug_authority.quote: Offering or undertaking to prescribe, order, give, or administer any drug or medicine for the use of another person

license_status_types.quote: The Board may issue an administrative medicine license to a physician who meets all qualifications for licensure

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates from schools listed in IMED must pass the ECFMG examination and the Federation of State Medical Boards examination. Graduates from schools not listed in IMED must also complete 3 years of postgraduate training in an ACGME-approved residency program. All foreign graduates must provide documentary proof that U.S./Canadian clinical rotations were in accredited institutions.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: A degree of Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathy, or an equivalent degree, from a legally incorporated medical college or school located in a country other than the United States or Canada, which medical college or school is not listed in the International Medical Education Directory (IMED), but the applicant has completed 3 years of postgraduate training in a residency program which has been approved by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education and has successfully passed the examination administered by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates and the Federation of State Medical Boards

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: A physician located outside the State who renders a written or otherwise documented medical opinion concerning the diagnosis or treatment of a person, or who actually renders treatment to a person within the State as a result of transmission of the person's medical data by electronic or other means, is considered to be practicing medicine in Delaware.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: Rendering a written or otherwise documented medical opinion concerning the diagnosis or treatment of a person or the actual rendering of treatment to a person within the State by a physician located outside the State as a result of transmission of the person's medical data by electronic or other means from within the State to the physician or to the physician's agent

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: "Collaborative agreement" means a written document expressing an arrangement of collaboration between a licensed physician and a physician assistant.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: Physician assistants have prescriptive authority for therapeutic drugs and treatments within the scope of physician assistant practice, subject to biennial renewal. They may also prescribe medication for termination of pregnancy including Mifeprex, Mifepristone, and Misoprostol. Temporarily licensed PAs may not have a prescriptive practice.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: Prescriptive authority for therapeutic drugs and treatments within the scope of physician assistant practice. The physician assistant's prescriptive authority and authority to practice as a physician assistant are subject to biennial renewal upon application to the Physician Assistant Regulatory Council

max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.quote: A collaborating physician may not at any given time collaborate with more than 4 physician assistants, unless a regulation of the Board increases or decreases the number.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: Every person to whom a certificate to practice medicine is issued has a duty to report to the Board, within 60 days, all information concerning medical malpractice claims settled or adjudicated to final judgment

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Every person to whom a certificate to practice medicine is issued and health care facility as defined in § 1740 of this title has a duty to report to the Board within 30 days: Any partial or full removal of hospital privileges based on adverse events, unprofessional conduct or competency issues

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: The Executive Director may defer the investigation of a report pending a reported licensee's evaluation and treatment for substance abuse or for physical or mental illness, provided sufficient safeguards exist to protect the licensee's patients and the public.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: If the Executive Director reasonably believes that a diagnostic mental or physical examination of the person under investigation is necessary, the Executive Director shall order the person to submit to an examination at the person's expense to be conducted by a physician or agency designated by the Executive Director.

administrative_medicine_license_availabl.quote: The Board may issue an administrative medicine license to a physician who meets all qualifications for licensure, including payment of a fee set by the Division of Professional Regulation, except that an applicant for an administrative medicine license shall not be required to show that the applicant has been engaged in the active practice of medicine

locum_tenens_permit_available.quote: The applicant for whom the examination is to be waived is licensed, certified, registered, or otherwise legally qualified to practice medicine in another state of the United States or in another jurisdiction, and seeks a temporary certificate to practice medicine for not less than 2 weeks nor more than 3 months for the purpose of taking charge of the practice of a person certified and registered to practice medicine in this State during the person's temporary illness or absence from this State.

scope__license_status_types.quote: The Board may establish, by class and not by individual, requirements for continuing education or reexamination, or both, for a person issued a certificate to practice medicine, or issued any authorized document to practice another profession or occupation regulated under this chapter, who is on inactive status and wishes to reactivate that person's status.

The Executive Director of the Board, with the approval of a physician member of the Board, may issue a temporary certificate pending certification to practice medicine for a period of time not to exceed 3 months to a person otherwise qualified to practice medicine who has applied for certification to practice medicine.
A certificate issued pursuant to this paragraph is subject to yearly renewal and restricts the applicant to practice only in the hospital or institution where the applicant is employed

A person to whom a certificate to practice medicine in this State has been issued may be disciplined by the Board for unprofessional conduct, as defined in subsection (b) of this section, by means of levying a fine, or by the restriction, suspension, or revocation, either permanent or temporary, of that person's certificate to practice medicine, or by other appropriate action
the restriction, suspension, or revocation, either permanent or temporary, of that person's certificate to practice medicine
The Board shall permanently revoke the certificate to practice medicine in this State of a person who is convicted of a felony sexual offense.

The applicant for whom the examination is to be waived: Is employed in this State as an intern, resident, house physician, or fellow in a hospital accredited by the Joint Commission on the Accreditation of Hospitals or by the American Osteopathic Hospital Association

The applicant for whom the examination is to be waived is licensed, certified, registered, or otherwise legally qualified to practice medicine in another state of the United States or in another jurisdiction, and seeks a temporary certificate to practice medicine for not less than 2 weeks nor more than 3 months for the purpose of taking charge of the practice of a person certified and registered to practice medicine in this State during the person's temporary illness or absence from this State.
